http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/04/soldi.text: Four people, including three civilians, were killed by an unidentified soldier in the Black Sea city of Sevastopol in Russian-annexed Crimea, the city's Moscow-installed governor said on Tuesday."A tragedy in Sevastopol...According to initial information, a soldier opened fire on his fellow servicemen, killing one person, before attacking civilians and killing three of them," Mikhail Razvozhayev wrote in a post on Telegram.He added the assailant, whose nationality was not specified and whose motives were not immediately clear, was arrested."Emergency services, investigators and forensic experts are currently working at the scene. All the circumstances and causes of what happened are being established," the Russian head of the city administration added.He also called on everyone to remain calm, trust only official information and not to spread unverified rumours.The civilian victims were two men aged 71 and 59, and a 64-year-old woman, Razvozhayev added.Crimea, a peninsula illegally annexed by Russia from Ukraine in 2014, has for weeks been the target of Ukrainian retaliatory attacks aimed at disrupting the logistics of Russian forces deployed in southern Ukraine.Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has regularly struck its neighbour, including from the Crimean peninsula.

https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Victorian treasurer highlights report that pokes holes in Coalition fiscal plan The Victorian treasurer, Colin Brooks, has this morning seized upon an Australia Institute discussion paper, released last night, which challenges the Coalition’s plan to return the state to a cash surplus by 2032. The paper said the centrepiece of the Coalition’s plan – to save $22bn via a hiring freeze across all back-office public service roles – would require the cutting of 31,700 jobs and could push unemployment toward 5.4%. “That would gut the public service. To claim this could be achieved with a few back office jobs is nonsense,” co-CEO Richard Denniss said. The paper also said the goal of returning the budget to cash surplus by 2032 would require cuts of government spending of at least $8bn each year, denying Victorians access to essential services and infrastructure.
